title: Fondant bow and ribbon
subtitle: rolled fondant shaped into a looped bow for decorating celebration cakes
excerpt: A fondant bow is made by rolling fondant into strips, folding them into loops, and supporting each loop with a roll of tissue while it dries. Once firm, the loops are assembled into a finished bow and placed on the cake. The technique works best with a fondant that holds its shape quickly and is often used on wedding and birthday cakes.
sourceNotes: Fondant bows and ribbons are a standard element of British sugarcraft taught in City and Guilds programmes from the 1970s onward, widely published in cake decorating books throughout the 1980s and 1990s.

content.text: A fondant bow is built from a set of loops, each made separately and left to firm before assembly. The fondant is rolled into a strip, looped into a teardrop shape and supported while it sets, and the dried loops are glued together with a dab of water or edible glue. Allow at least 24 hours from start to placement on the cake.
Colour the fondant as needed. Roll to about 3 mm thick on a surface dusted lightly with cornflour. For a glossy, satin-like finish, roll between two sheets of baking paper.
Cut strips about 2 cm wide and 12 cm long for the loops. The strip length controls the loop size. For a larger bow, cut longer strips.

Brush one end of each strip with a tiny amount of water. Fold into a loop, pressing the two ends together at the centre. Support the loop upright with a tight roll of kitchen paper pushed inside while it dries. Make 6 to 8 loops per bow.
Leave the loops to dry for at least 12 hours. They must be fully firm before assembly; partially set loops will collapse under their own weight.
Cut two ribbon tails: strips about 2 cm wide, cut at an angle at one end. Attach these first to the cake or board with a dab of edible glue, arranging them to fall naturally.
Arrange the loops in a circle on top of the tails, pinching the base of each loop together at the centre. Press a small round of fondant over the join to cover the pinched ends and secure.

attrs.avoid: Avoid fondant that is too soft; it sags and loses its shape before setting.
attrs.fix: Knead in a small amount of CMC (tylose powder), which speeds up the drying time significantly. Support every loop with a paper roll while it dries.

attrs.problem: Loops cracking and breaking on assembly
attrs.avoid: Avoid handling loops before they are fully dry; they are fragile when partially set.
attrs.fix: Leave for a full 24 hours before touching. Fondant bows can be made 3 to 4 days in advance and stored in an open container at room temperature.
